sections.name: lateral
sections.sig:
< lateral (L 1800 [cm])
                (x x )
                (rad 3.5 [cm])
                (height height )
                (pipe position -110 [cm])
                (eq depth eq depth )              ; Default MolenWesseling value.
                (pipe outlet pipe outlet )        ; Default deep value.
                (K to pipes K to pipes )
                (pipe level pipe level ) >

attrs.name: x
attrs.doc: Horizontal distance to nearest pipe. By default, this is 1/2 L.

attrs.name: pipe position
attrs.doc: Height pipes are placed in the soil (a negative number).

attrs.name: eq depth
attrs.doc:
Component (default ‘MolenWesseling’)
     Model for calculating equivalent depth for drains.

attrs.name: pipe outlet
attrs.doc:
Component (default ‘deep’)
        Water table in drain pipe outlet.
        By default this will be identical to ‘pipe position’, meaning free flow of water
        through drains. Specifying a lower water level will not affect the simulation.
        Specifying a higher water level is functionally equivalent to temporarily in-
        creasing the ’pipe position’, lowering the ability of the drain system to drain
        the soil.
        Currently, there is no posibility of water flowing from the pipe outlet to soil.

attrs.name: K to pipes
attrs.doc:
Horizontal conductivity in saturated soil. By default this is calculated from
        the horizontal conductivity and the anisotropy of the horizon.

attrs.name: pipe level
attrs.doc:
Current effective pipe position (a negative number).
Log Variables

sections.text:
Pipe drainage. See also [Hooghoudt, 1940]
  < lateral (L 1800 [cm])
                (x x )
                (rad 3.5 [cm])
                (height height )
                (pipe position -110 [cm])
                (eq depth eq depth )              ; Default MolenWesseling value.
                (pipe outlet pipe outlet )        ; Default deep value.
                (K to pipes K to pipes )
                (pipe level pipe level ) >

    L: number [cm]
     Parameter (default 1800)
     Distance between pipes.

    x : number [cm]
     Optional parameter
     Horizontal distance to nearest pipe. By default, this is 1/2 L.

    rad : number [cm]
     Parameter (default 3.5)
     Inner radius of drain pipes.

    height: number [cm]
     Optional state variable
     Current groundwater level (a negative number).

    pipe position: number [cm]
     Parameter (default -110)
     Height pipes are placed in the soil (a negative number).

    eq depth: draineqd component (see chapter 38)
     Component (default ‘MolenWesseling’)
     Model for calculating equivalent depth for drains.

       pipe outlet: depth component (see chapter 34)
        Component (default ‘deep’)
        Water table in drain pipe outlet.
        By default this will be identical to ‘pipe position’, meaning free flow of water
        through drains. Specifying a lower water level will not affect the simulation.
        Specifying a higher water level is functionally equivalent to temporarily in-
        creasing the ’pipe position’, lowering the ability of the drain system to drain
        the soil.
        Currently, there is no posibility of water flowing from the pipe outlet to soil.

       K to pipes: number [cm/h]
        Optional parameter
        Horizontal conductivity in saturated soil. By default this is calculated from
        the horizontal conductivity and the anisotropy of the horizon.

       pipe level : number [cm]
        Optional state variable
        Current effective pipe position (a negative number).

Log Variables
       S : number [cm3 /cm3 /h] soil cells
        Pipe drainage.
       DrainFlow : number [cm/h]
        Drain flow to pipes.

       EqDrnFlow : number [cm/h]
        Equilibrium drain flow to pipes.

sections.name: none
sections.text:
No lateral transport.
   Used by column default Drain (see 26.1, page 153) .
